# TUNING — Assignment 6

All strips are **fixture captures**. Each is a preview scene rendered by Movie Maker at 30 fps, with a fixed seed set on the preview's own instance only. Setup: Godot 4.7.2, Forward+, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU, 1280 × 720.

Each revision below records five things:
- what I saw in the running game;
- Claude's reading of the strip before the change;
- the change itself, which I approved;
- Claude's prediction for the new strip, and its comparison of the new strip with that prediction;
- my verdict in the running game.

## 2026-11-06 — Effect A, r0 (first strip, before any tuning)

**Strip:** `captures/cover_hit_burst/r0/` — frames 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 50 (fixture).

**Capture log:** `logs/capture_cover_hit_burst_r0.log`. It shows the device NVIDIA RTX 3060 Laptop, and one burst at frame 10 at (600.7, 349.15), rotation −π (pointing back out of the left face).

**My first look** (preview window, 1280 × 720, before any Claude read the strip), in my own words:

> 闪光看得见，正好。砖块主要往左侧飞，也不错。看得清，大小合适。大概一两秒没有了。

(English: The flash is visible and about right. The chips fly mainly to the left, which is good. It is readable and the size is right. It is gone after about one or two seconds.)

**My second look** (preview window, after viewing my own strip, before any Claude reading):

> 看得清。

(English: The chips are readable against the ground.)

Checked against the strip: the burst is gone by frame 50 (1.33 s) and only faint dust is left at frame 30 (0.67 s), so my "one or two seconds" overestimated the duration (brief R2.4).

**In the running game** (main scene, 1280 × 720, NVIDIA RTX 3060, 2026-11-06; Effect A wired in at d2d50fc). I played for a few minutes and shot at cover.

- **Four hits on one wall until it broke** — checked. Every hit was visible.
- **Firing while moving** — checked. The chips read against the ground.
- **Chips go back toward the shooter** — not checked separately.
- **Pause right after a hit** — not checked here (to be checked with Effect B's edge checks).
- **My verdict:**

  > 游戏一切都正常。真的没有想改的地方。

  (English: Everything works in the game. There is nothing I want changed.)

So **no revision of Effect A is driven by something I observed in the running game**. The revision below (r1) comes from Claude's reading of the r0 strip. My verdict in the running game decides whether it is kept or rejected.

1	extends Node2D
2	## Frame-strip fixture for Effect A (CHANGE-BRIEF.md, Effect A "The frame strip"). Preview only:
3	## changes no game script. One real cover block (scripts/cover.gd, world = null, never hit) on the
4	## real ground tile, camera at (640, 360), zoom 1. The burst sits where a shell flying right
5	## (dir (1, 0)) touches the block's left face, drawn at shell.gd's DRAW_OFFSET, rotated to
6	## (-dir).angle() = PI, as main.gd's spawn_cover_burst() will place it.
7	## Frame numbers are Engine.get_frames_drawn(), which equals the Movie Maker frame number.
8	
9	const BURST := preload("res://effects/cover_hit_burst.tscn")
10	const COVER_HALF_WIDTH := 36.3  # cover.gd: RectangleShape2D 72.6 x 22
11	const SHELL_RADIUS := 3.0  # shell.gd: CircleShape2D radius
12	const DRAW_OFFSET := Vector2(0.0, -10.85)  # shell.gd line 5
13	const SHELL_DIR := Vector2(1, 0)
14	const FIRST_FRAME := 10
15	const RETRIGGER_FRAME := 16
16	
17	## Second burst at frame 16 (0.2 s later, inside one lifetime), for the overlap read.
18	@export var retrigger := false
19	## Fixed seed for this preview's instances only; the effect scene never sets one.
20	@export var fixed_seed := 7
21	
22	@onready var cover: Node2D = $Cover
23	@onready var fx: Node2D = $FX
24	
25	var _fired := {}
26	
27	
28	func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
29		var f := Engine.get_frames_drawn()
30		if f >= FIRST_FRAME and not _fired.has(FIRST_FRAME):
31			_fired[FIRST_FRAME] = true
32			_spawn(fixed_seed, f)
33		if retrigger and f >= RETRIGGER_FRAME and not _fired.has(RETRIGGER_FRAME):
34			_fired[RETRIGGER_FRAME] = true
35			_spawn(fixed_seed + 1, f)
36	
37	
38	func _spawn(seed_value: int, frame: int) -> void:
39		var contact := cover.global_position + Vector2(-COVER_HALF_WIDTH - SHELL_RADIUS, 0.0)
40		var burst := BURST.instantiate()
41		burst.global_position = contact + DRAW_OFFSET
42		burst.rotation = (-SHELL_DIR).angle()
43		var emitters := []
44		for c in burst.get_children():
45			if c is CPUParticles2D:
46				c.use_fixed_seed = true
47				c.seed = seed_value
48				emitters.append(c)
49		fx.add_child(burst)
50		for e in emitters:
51			e.restart()  # restart after the seed is set, so the seed is used for this emission
52		print("preview: burst (seed %d) at frame %d, position %s, rotation %.4f" % [seed_value, frame, burst.global_position, burst.rotation])
53

content.text:
I read all six r0 frames at full size (1280 × 720). I tried to crop and enlarge them with a short Python script, but that needed approval in this session, so I didn't measure any pixels. Every position, size and colour below is my estimate by eye from the full frames. The burst sits at (600.7, 349.15), on the left end of the cover block, rotated −π, so the chips fly left over the open ground.

## What each frame shows

| Frame | Time | What I see |
|---|---|---|
| **10** | 0 s | A bright cream-white disc about 45 px across, centred on the block's left end and spilling over the brick. Its edge looks almost hard. **No chips are visible**: they are still inside the 4 px emission sphere, pale #E8D8B0 on a near-white flash. There is no dust yet. |
| **12** | 0.07 s | The flash is still near full brightness and about the same size. A thin crescent of small pale peach chips sits on its left edge, only about 10–20 px out. No dust is separate from the flash yet. |
| **15** | 0.17 s | The flash is gone. A pale sand dust puff about 25–30 px across sits on the block's left end. About 20 chips, now orange-red, sit in a wide arc 25–50 px left of the impact point, spread about ±40 px up and down. This is the best frame for the chips: they read clearly against the dark ground. |
| **20** | 0.33 s | The dust is now the main element: about 45–50 px across, pale, partly over the brick. **The chips have almost disappeared.** I can find only a few faint dark-red specks around x ≈ 545–575. |
| **30** | 0.67 s | A very faint grey haze to the upper left of the block. No chips. |
| **50** | 1.33 s | Nothing left; the block is clean. |

## Comparison with the intent block

1. **Timing, dissipation phase (chips).** The brief's frame-20 row says "chips almost stopped, about 2 hull widths out, red-brown and smaller". In r0 the chips are nearly invisible by frame 20, so they read on screen only from about frame 12 to frame 17 (0.2 s).
   - The ramp explains it. At frame 20 a chip is at 0.55 of its life, so its colour sits between `#B5523A a1 @0.3` and `#5A3A2E a0 @1`: alpha is about 0.64, the colour is dark brown, and the chip is 2.4–4.8 px.
   - The fade starts at 0.3 of life, which is 0.18 s. That is inside the brief's *outward* phase, not in dissipation.
2. **Contrast.** This confirms R2.2 in the strip. #5A3A2E has a luma of about 66. By eye the ground is about the same, roughly 60–65. Chips on their last colour are therefore the same value as the ground, and frame 20 shows them vanishing.
3. **Change over life, chips.** "→ brick red → dark brown, then fade" shows up as red, then gone. Neither the dark-brown step nor the shrink to 40 % is ever seen.
4. **Timing, impact → outward (flash).** At frame 12 the flash still looks almost as bright as at frame 10. Three additive sprites at about 0.44 alpha each still saturate on cream, so "the flash fading" in the frame-12 row isn't visible. The flash then disappears between frames 12 and 15. This is minor.
5. **Layering at frame 10.** "Chips already leaving the point" isn't visible: the flash covers the chips. This is minor.
6. **Scale.** The flash is about 45 px, which R2.3 already accepts. The dust ends at about 45–50 px, roughly 1.5 hull widths, as specified. The chips should travel about 55 px by frame 20 (worked from 180–320 px/s and 400–600 damping), close to the 2 hull widths in the brief. But they are invisible by the time they get there, so on screen they reach only about 50 px (frame 15).
7. **Fan shape.** At frame 15 the chips form a tall arc, about 80 px high and 50 px deep, rather than a fan aimed back along the shell's path. That is the 120° fan R2.1 accepted.
8. **Variation.** It can't be judged from this strip: one fixed-seed burst, `retrigger` off. ±0.03 hue on 3–7 px chips isn't visible. Your four-hits-on-one-wall check is the evidence for this one.
9. **Dust** matches the brief at every frame.

**The difference that matters most is #1 (with #2 and #3 as its cause).** The chips are the only layer that says *the wall lost material, and in which direction*. The flash and dust only say "something happened here". In r0 that message lasts about 0.2 s instead of about 0.5 s, and the reason is the colour stop R2.2 already flagged as too close to the ground's value.

This doesn't contradict your verdicts. You judged the chips readable, and they are while they're red, at frames 12–17. The strip shows they don't reach the brief's dissipation phase.

## Proposed change (one setting): Debris `color_ramp`

| | Value |
|---|---|
| **Brief value replaced** (Debris `color_ramp`, settings table) | `#E8D8B0 a1 @0 → #B5523A a1 @0.3 → #5A3A2E a0 @1` |
| **Proposed** | `#E8D8B0 a1 @0 → #B5523A a1 @0.3 → #8E5040 a1 @0.6 → #8E5040 a0 @1` |

- **Lighter end colour.** #8E5040 has a luma of about 97: darker than #B5523A (about 108), so the chips still "darken", but well above the ground (about 63, by eye). It is roughly the shade of the brick block in the frame.
- **Alpha held until 0.6 of life.** The fade then falls in 0.36–0.6 s, inside the brief's 0.3–0.7 s dissipation phase.
- **Brief text this also changes:** "Change over life" says "→ dark brown" (it would become "→ dull brick brown"). `tests/test_cover_hit_burst_config.gd` line 49 asserts the old three stops, so it would need the new four.

The Debris `scale_amount_curve`, velocities, damping and lifetime stay the same, as do Flash and Dust. The cost is unchanged, because the change adds no particles.

## Predicted r1 strip

Same seed. The ramp doesn't consume any random values, so every chip should be in the same place at the same size.

| Frame | Predicted difference from r0 |
|---|---|
| 10 | Identical: life 0, same colour, hidden under the flash. |
| 12 | Identical: life 0.11, still before the first stop. |
| 15 | Practically identical: life 0.28 is almost exactly #B5523A, alpha 1. |
| **20** | **The main change.** About 20 chips are visible, opaque (alpha 1.0 instead of about 0.64), red-brown (about #964D3E instead of a muddy #8A4434 at 64 %). They are 2.4–4.8 px and about 50–60 px left of the impact point (x ≈ 540–575), in the same arc as frame 15 but wider and more spread out. This matches the brief's frame-20 row. |
| (25, not in the strip) | Chips at about 40 % alpha, fading. |
| 30 | Identical: chips died at frame 28 (lifetime 0.6 s), faint dust only. |
| 50 | Identical: empty. |

Overall, the chips should read from frame 12 to about frame 25 instead of about frame 17. The burst should still be gone by 0.7 s.

What r1 might show instead: if the frame-20 chips still don't stand out at 2.4–4.8 px, the limit is chip size rather than colour. The next change would then be the Debris `scale_amount_curve` end value (0.4), which this proposal deliberately leaves alone.

I haven't edited or committed anything.
